newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan sends trade team to Iraq, claims large sales.
newsitem.headline: Jordan sends trade team to Iraq, claims large sales.

text.p: Jordan sent a senior economic team to Iraq on Sunday to promote trade as businessmen boasted of over $80 million in orders under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.

The delegation led by Finance Minister Marwan Awad and Energy Minister Hashem Dabbas is the most senior Jordanian mission to Iraq since King Hussein last year turned on President Saddam Hussein after years of close ties.

Officials say the visit is part of a Jordanian effort to gain from the $2 billion oil-for-food deal launched this month. It faces competition from Turkey, Gulf states and foreign businessmen also seeking to sell Iraq products allowed under the U.N. deal.
The visit will pave the way for a Jordanian-Iraqi economic committee headed by the two trade ministers to meet during the first week of January, officials said.
Jordan has made conciliatory gestures towards Iraq since announcement of the oil-for food deal as its businessmen clamour for government support to expand business ties.

Khaldoun Abu-Hassan, head of the Amman Chamber of Industry, a powerful pro-Iraq lobby, told Reuters firms had won orders to supply Iraq with goods worth $82 million in competitive bids under the oil-for-food accord.
The goods were mostly detergent, soap, table salt and vegetable oil. Another $20 million in Iraqi orders, almost concluded, are for Jordanian pharmaceuticals.

The Jordanian visit is expected to renew the annual trade protocol under which Jordan gets all its oil in return for industrial goods, officials said. Half the $400 million value of the oil goes toward settling over $1 billion of accumulated Iraqi debts.

Jordan gets about 75,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude oil and petroleum products. Officials privately say the team will discuss extra oil imports that could raise the value of trade under their protocol.

The business community wants to restore the protocol to at least $400 million, where it stood in 1995. Most of Jordan's industrial exports to Iraq go through the protocol and Jordanian businessmen say Baghdad is ready to expand it.
Jordan's businessmen feel vindicated for resisting pressure to curb ties with Baghdad and look to Israel. They say Iraq is Jordan's natural market.
